bug_info.bug_desc: During a G-stage intermediate page-table walk, the PTW incorrectly applies the original instruction-fetch permission rule to the intermediate translation result by requiring execute permission on the PTE. This can raise a spurious page-fault exception for an intermediate G-stage page-table access, even though the walk is translating a page-table memory access rather than completing the original instruction fetch.
bug_info.fix_hint: When the current PTW stage is the G-stage intermediate stage, do not require execute permission solely because the original request was an instruction fetch. Keep the required PTE validity and access checks for the page-table walk, but distinguish intermediate G-stage page-table accesses from final instruction-fetch translations.

bug_info.bug_desc: During a G-stage intermediate page-table walk for a data-side request, the PTW incorrectly applies final load/store permission handling to the intermediate translation result. In particular, a store-triggered walk can be faulted because the intermediate G-stage entry does not satisfy final store write/dirty requirements, even though the intermediate access is a page-table memory translation rather than the final store access.
bug_info.fix_hint: When forming the data-side permission condition, treat the G-stage intermediate stage as a page-table walk access and exempt it from final store write/dirty requirements. Preserve the normal permission checks for final S-stage or G-stage translations.

bug_info.bug_desc: After the data-side permission condition succeeds, the PTW performs a separate post-check for store requests that unconditionally faults when the PTE lacks write or dirty permission. This post-check also runs during G-stage intermediate page-table walks, so it can override the intended intermediate-stage behavior and force a spurious page-fault exception for store-triggered nested translation walks.
bug_info.fix_hint: Remove or fold the separate store write/dirty post-check into the main permission condition so that it is not applied to G-stage intermediate page-table walks. Store write/dirty requirements should only affect final translations where the PTE authorizes the original store access.
